answer: After LiveMonitor.kill, remote workers keep appending REMOTE_COMPLETED to the durable JSONL ledger and to an independent remote-jobs.json. recover() folds the ledger with no RAM context and harvests A,B; C was harvested before death; D stays in-flight. Reconciliation against the remote job list loaded from disk yields unknown_count=0 for every unit the remote side considers finished. An uninterrupted twin run also yields unknown_count=0 (both-states). A memory-only mutant that records A,B terminal state only in the live process is detected: after restart those ids are UNKNOWN against the same remote job list, while a check that trusted the pre-kill RAM snapshot would have passed silently.
claim_under_test: Durable ledger + independent remote job list recover every remote-finished unit after monitor death; RAM-only terminal state is reported UNKNOWN by the same reconciler.

evidence.claim: Signal (a): post-restart recover() on the JSONL ledger harvests A,B (finished during the outage), keeps C harvested, leaves D in-flight, and reconciliation reports unknown_count=0. Signal (b): remote-jobs.json is a second file whose sha256 differs from the ledger; it lists A,B,C as succeeded when queried from disk after restart. The uninterrupted twin also reports unknown_count=0.
